source.text: Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὁ μὴ εἰσερχόμενος διὰ τῆς θύρας εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τῶν προβάτων ἀλλὰ ἀναβαίνων ἀλλαχόθεν ἐκεῖνος κλέπτης ἐστὶν καὶ λῃστής·

records.literal_gloss: "Truly truly I say to you, the [one] not entering through the door into the fold of the sheep but going up from elsewhere, that one a thief is and a bandit;

en.L: "Truly, truly I say to you, the one who does not enter through the door into the fold of the sheep, but climbs up from elsewhere, that one is a thief and a bandit.
en.B: "Truly, truly, I tell you, anyone who does not go into the sheepfold by the door, but climbs in from somewhere else, is a thief and a bandit.
en.R: "I tell you the truth: anyone who does not go into the sheep pen through the door, but climbs over the wall somewhere else, is a thief and a bandit.

es.L: «En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que el que no entra por la puerta en el redil de las ovejas, sino que sube por otra parte, ese es ladrón y bandido.
es.B: «En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que quien no entra en el redil por la puerta, sino que se mete por otro lado, es un ladrón y un bandido.
es.R: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: quien no entra en el corral de las ovejas por la puerta, sino que salta el muro por otro lado, es un ladrón y un bandido.

fr.L: « En vérité, en vérité, je vous le dis : celui qui n’entre pas par la porte dans l’enclos des brebis, mais qui monte par un autre endroit, celui-là est un voleur et un bandit.
fr.B: « En vérité, en vérité, je vous le dis : celui qui n’entre pas dans l’enclos des brebis par la porte, mais qui grimpe pour entrer par un autre côté, est un voleur et un bandit.
fr.R: « Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : celui qui n’entre pas dans l’enclos des brebis par la porte, mais qui passe par-dessus le mur à un autre endroit, est un voleur et un bandit.

sw.L: "Kweli kweli nawaambia, yule asiyeingia kupitia mlango katika zizi la kondoo, bali anapanda kupitia njia nyingine, huyo ni mwizi na mnyang'anyi.
sw.B: "Kweli kweli nawaambia, mtu yeyote asiyeingia zizini kupitia mlango, bali anapanda kuingia kupitia upande mwingine, ni mwizi na mnyang'anyi.
sw.R: "Nawaambia ukweli: mtu yeyote asiyeingia katika zizi la kondoo kupitia mlango, bali anapanda ukuta mahali pengine, ni mwizi na mnyang'anyi.

vi.L: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, kẻ nào không đi qua cửa mà vào chuồng chiên, nhưng trèo lên từ chỗ khác, kẻ ấy là kẻ trộm và kẻ cướp.
vi.B: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, ai không vào chuồng chiên bằng cửa mà trèo vào từ lối khác, người ấy là kẻ trộm và kẻ cướp.
vi.R: "Ta nói thật với các người: ai không vào chuồng chiên bằng cửa, mà trèo qua tường ở chỗ khác, người đó là kẻ trộm, kẻ cướp.

ko.L: "진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 문을 통하여 양들의 우리 안으로 들어가지 않고 다른 데로 올라가는 사람, 그 사람은 도둑이고 강도이다.
ko.B: "진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 양 우리에 문으로 들어가지 않고 다른 곳을 타고 넘어 들어가는 사람은 도둑이고 강도다.
ko.R: "내가 분명히 말한다. 양 우리에 문으로 들어가지 않고 다른 곳에서 담을 넘어 들어가는 사람은 도둑이고 강도다.

decisions.choice: the speech goes straight on from 9:41: "you" are the Pharisees of 9:40-41
alternatives: a new speech to a new audience
decisions.reason: There is no change of place, time or listeners between 9:41 and 10:1; the chapter division is later than the text. Jesus has just told the Pharisees who claim to see that their sin remains (9:41), and he goes on speaking to them (10:6 says he spoke "to them"). The picture of the shepherd and the thieves follows directly on their treatment of the man who was healed and thrown out (9:34).

decisions.choice: the fold: a walled enclosure for sheep with a single entrance
alternatives: the courtyard of a house only
decisions.reason: The word means an enclosed yard. Sheepfolds were enclosures with walls of stone, often topped with thorns, and one opening; sometimes the yard of a house served. The sheep were kept there at night. Anyone who came in over the wall instead of through the entrance had no right to be there. The same word is used for the courtyard of the high priest (18:15).

decisions.choice: thief: one who steals by stealth; bandit: one who robs by violence
alternatives: two words for the same person with no difference
decisions.reason: The two words are not the same. The first is the ordinary word for a thief, used of Judas (12:6). The second is a robber who uses force, the kind who attacked travelers on the road (Luke 10:30); it is also the word for Barabbas (18:40), and in the first century it was used of armed rebels. Together they describe someone who takes what is not his, by cunning or by force.

decisions.choice: the shepherd picture draws on Ezekiel 34, Jeremiah 23:1-4 and Psalm 23
decisions.reason: The Scriptures often call Israel God's flock and its leaders shepherds. Ezekiel 34 condemns the shepherds of Israel who fed themselves and scattered the sheep, and promises that God himself will seek his sheep and set one shepherd, his servant David, over them (Ezekiel 34:11-16, 23). Jeremiah 23:1-4 pronounces woe on shepherds who destroy and scatter the flock. Psalm 23 calls God the shepherd who leads his sheep to pasture. That the thieves and bandits here are meant as the false shepherds of Ezekiel 34, in the persons of the Pharisees who threw the man out (9:34), is likely from the setting but not stated; the verbal links are clearer in 10:11-16.

decisions.choice: Truly, truly I say to you (L); Truly, truly, I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage; it covers 10:7 as well.

decisions.choice: the fold of the sheep (L); the sheepfold (B); the sheep pen (R); a thief and a bandit at every level
decisions.reason: "Bandit" keeps the two Greek words distinct (meaning decision m3) and is used again in 10:8. "Door" is kept at every level so that "I am the door" (10:7, 9) is heard as the same word.

decisions.choice: climbs over the wall somewhere else
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what climbing in "from elsewhere" means in a walled fold (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: En verdad, en verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide Spanish rendering, recorded once in this passage; it covers 10:7. Jesus speaks to the Pharisees of 9:40-41, so every plural "you" is the ustedes / vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: redil (L, B); corral de las ovejas (R); ladrón y bandido at every level
decisions.reason: "Bandido" keeps the two Greek words apart (meaning decision m3) and returns in 10:8; "salteador" is now old. "Puerta" is kept at every level, since Jesus takes up the word in 10:7-9.

decisions.choice: salta el muro
decisions.reason: As in English: says what climbing in "by another way" means in a walled fold (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: En vérité, en vérité, je vous le dis (L, B); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R)
alternatives: Amen, amen, je vous le dis
Oui, vraiment, je vous le dis
decisions.reason: The book-wide French rendering for John, recorded once in this passage; it covers 10:7 as well. Readable puts the pledge in plain words.

decisions.choice: la porte; l’enclos des brebis; les brebis; un voleur et un bandit
decisions.reason: "Porte" at every level, so that "je suis la porte" (10:7, 9) is heard as the same word. "Brebis" is the usual French word for the sheep of a flock in this picture and is used through chapter 10. The two words for wrongdoers are kept apart (meaning decision m3): "voleur" for one who steals by stealth, "bandit" for one who robs by force, as the English does; "bandit" returns in 10:8. "Enclos" rather than "bergerie" for the yard at every level, as in 10:16: "bergerie" suggests a covered farm building.

decisions.choice: zizi (fold); mwizi na mnyang'anyi (thief and bandit)
decisions.reason: "Zizi" is the walled enclosure where flocks were kept at night, the picture in the meaning note. "Mwizi" steals by stealth and "mnyang'anyi" robs by force, so the two Greek words stay distinct.

decisions.choice: "진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 분명히 말한다" (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide Korean rendering of amen amen (style guide, section 6), recorded once for this passage. The archaic ending -노니 is avoided; Readable keeps the force of the solemn formula in plain words.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to the Pharisees in the plain style (해라체: "말한다", "도둑이다")
decisions.reason: The style guide sets 해라체 for Jesus speaking to disciples, crowds and opponents; it holds through this discourse (10:1-18) so that the relationship does not change between verses.

decisions.choice: "도둑" (thief) and "강도" (bandit) at every level
decisions.reason: The two Greek words differ as stealth and violence; Korean "도둑" and "강도" keep the same difference in everyday words.

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, Ta nói với các người" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các người" (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of amen amen for this passage: the doubled word kept at L and B, folded into "nói thật" at R. "Ta" is Jesus's self-reference throughout (deity_pronoun span in mid-sentence).

decisions.choice: "các người" for "you" (the Pharisees of 9:40-41)
decisions.reason: Style guide section 6: Jesus addresses crowds, opponents and officials as "các người", which is direct without being rude; kept through 10:1-18 and 10:25-38.

decisions.choice: "chuồng chiên" for the fold; "kẻ trộm" and "kẻ cướp" for thief and bandit
decisions.reason: "chuồng chiên" is the plain modern word for a sheep enclosure; "ràn" is regional and old-fashioned. "kẻ trộm" (stealth) and "kẻ cướp" (violence) keep the two kinds of thief apart.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἰσερχόμενος διὰ τῆς θύρας ποιμήν ἐστιν τῶν προβάτων.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] but entering through the door shepherd is of the sheep.

en.L: But the one who enters through the door is [the] shepherd of the sheep.
en.B: But the one who goes in through the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
en.R: But the one who goes in through the door is the shepherd of the sheep.

es.L: Pero el que entra por la puerta es [el] pastor de las ovejas.
es.B: Pero el que entra por la puerta es el pastor de las ovejas.
es.R: Pero el que entra por la puerta es el pastor de las ovejas.

fr.L: Mais celui qui entre par la porte est [le] berger des brebis.
fr.B: Mais celui qui entre par la porte est le berger des brebis.
fr.R: Mais celui qui entre par la porte est le berger des brebis.

sw.L: Lakini anayeingia kupitia mlango ni mchungaji wa kondoo.
sw.B: Lakini yule anayeingia kupitia mlango ndiye mchungaji wa kondoo.
sw.R: Lakini yule anayeingia kupitia mlango ndiye mchungaji wa kondoo.

vi.L: Còn người đi qua cửa mà vào là người chăn chiên.
vi.B: Nhưng người đi vào qua cửa mới là người chăn chiên.
vi.R: Nhưng người đi vào qua cửa mới là người chăn chiên.

ko.L: 그러나 문을 통하여 들어가는 사람은 양들의 목자이다.
ko.R: 하지만 문으로 들어가는 사람은 양들의 목자다.

decisions.choice: shepherd without the article: he is the one with a right to the sheep, the shepherd as opposed to a thief
alternatives: the one Good Shepherd already named
decisions.reason: The Greek has no article with "shepherd". The point is the contrast with verse 1: whoever comes by the door shows himself a shepherd, not a thief. At this stage of the picture the shepherd is not yet identified; Jesus names himself the good shepherd in 10:11.

decisions.choice: entering through the door: coming openly by the rightful way
alternatives: a reference to Jesus as the door (10:7)
decisions.reason: In the picture the door is simply the proper entrance, opened for the shepherd by the doorkeeper (verse 3). Only in 10:7 does Jesus apply the door to himself, in a second step of the picture.

decisions.choice: [the] shepherd
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the article English needs (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: [el] pastor
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal brackets the article (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "들어가는 사람이라야 ... 목자다" (only the one who goes in ... is the shepherd)
decisions.reason: The Korean ending -이라야 carries both the contrast ("but") with the thief of 10:1 and the point of the anarthrous "shepherd": he is the one with a right to the sheep.

decisions.choice: "mới là" (is the one who really is)
decisions.reason: "mới là" carries the contrast the meaning decision describes: he, and not the thief, is the shepherd; Vietnamese needs no article for this.

source.text: τούτῳ ὁ θυρωρὸς ἀνοίγει, καὶ τὰ πρόβατα τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούει καὶ τὰ ἴδια πρόβατα φωνεῖ κατ’ ὄνομα καὶ ἐξάγει αὐτά.

records.literal_gloss: To this [one] the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep the voice of him hear, and the own sheep he calls by name and leads out them.

en.L: For this one the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep hear his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
en.B: For him the doorkeeper opens the door, and the sheep hear his voice. He calls each of his own sheep by name and leads them out.
en.R: The one who keeps watch at the door opens it for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls each of his own sheep by name and leads them out.

es.L: A este el portero le abre, y las ovejas oyen su voz, y llama a sus propias ovejas por nombre y las saca.
es.B: A él el portero le abre la puerta, y las ovejas oyen su voz. Llama a cada una de sus ovejas por su nombre y las saca.
es.R: El que cuida la puerta le abre, y las ovejas escuchan su voz. Él llama a cada una de sus ovejas por su nombre y las saca.

fr.L: À celui-ci le portier ouvre, et les brebis entendent sa voix, et il appelle ses propres brebis par [leur] nom et les fait sortir.
fr.B: Le portier lui ouvre la porte, et les brebis écoutent sa voix. Il appelle chacune de ses brebis par son nom et les fait sortir.
fr.R: Celui qui garde la porte lui ouvre, et les brebis écoutent sa voix. Il appelle chacune de ses brebis par son nom et il les fait sortir.

sw.L: Huyu bawabu humfungulia, na kondoo huisikia sauti yake, naye huwaita kondoo wake mwenyewe kwa majina na kuwaongoza nje.
sw.B: Bawabu humfungulia mlango, na kondoo huisikia sauti yake. Huwaita kondoo wake mwenyewe kila mmoja kwa jina lake, na kuwaongoza nje.
sw.R: Mlinzi wa mlango humfungulia, na kondoo huisikiliza sauti yake. Huwaita kondoo wake mwenyewe kila mmoja kwa jina, na kuwaongoza nje.

vi.L: Người giữ cửa mở cho người ấy, và chiên nghe tiếng người, và người gọi đích danh chiên của riêng mình và dẫn chúng ra.
vi.B: Người giữ cửa mở cửa cho người, và chiên nghe tiếng người. Người gọi tên từng con chiên của mình và dẫn chúng ra ngoài.
vi.R: Người canh cửa mở cửa cho người chăn, và chiên lắng nghe tiếng người. Người gọi tên từng con chiên của mình rồi dẫn chúng ra ngoài.

ko.L: 문지기는 이 사람에게 [문을] 열어 주고, 양들은 그의 음성을 듣는다. 그는 자기 양들을 이름으로 부르고 그들을 밖으로 이끌어 낸다.
ko.B: 문지기는 그에게 문을 열어 주고, 양들은 그의 목소리를 알아듣는다. 그는 자기 양들을 하나하나 이름을 불러 밖으로 데리고 나간다.
ko.R: 문을 지키는 사람이 그에게 문을 열어 준다. 양들은 그의 목소리에 귀를 기울인다. 그는 자기 양들을 하나하나 이름으로 부르고 밖으로 데리고 나간다.

decisions.choice: the doorkeeper: a watchman who guarded the entrance of the fold
alternatives: a figure for some particular person
decisions.reason: Where several flocks shared one fold for the night, a watchman kept the entrance and opened it in the morning to the shepherds he knew. The doorkeeper is part of the scene and is not explained in the passage; nothing in the text says whom he stands for.

decisions.choice: his own sheep: his flock among others in the same fold
alternatives: all the sheep in the fold
decisions.reason: The phrase "his own" sets his sheep apart from others kept in the fold. He calls each of his own by name, and those are the ones he leads out (10:14, 27).

decisions.choice: hear his voice: listen and respond to him
decisions.reason: Hearing a voice in John is responding to the one who speaks (5:25; 10:16, 27; 18:37). The sheep know whose voice it is and answer it.

decisions.choice: leads out: perhaps an echo of God leading his people out of Egypt and of Numbers 27:17
alternatives: an ordinary word for taking sheep out to pasture, with no echo
decisions.reason: The verb is the ordinary one for leading out. In the Greek Old Testament it is used of God bringing Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 20:2) and in Moses's prayer for a leader who will lead the people out and bring them in, so that they are not like sheep without a shepherd (Numbers 27:16-17). Whether John intends the echo here is uncertain.

decisions.choice: his, he, him for the shepherd in 10:1-5 written without a deity_pronoun span; pronouns for Jesus from 10:6 on take one
alternatives: capitalisable pronouns for the shepherd in the picture
decisions.reason: In 10:1-5 Jesus tells a picture (10:6), and the shepherd is a figure in it, like the bridegroom of 3:29; his pronouns are not pronouns for God or Christ. When Jesus applies the picture to himself from 10:7 ("I am the door"), and when the narrator speaks of him (10:6), the pronouns for Jesus take the usual span.

decisions.choice: opens the door (B); opens it (R); calls each of his own sheep by name (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what is opened; Readable also describes the doorkeeper's work instead of using the title. "Each" brings out that the Greek phrase means name by name.

decisions.choice: pronouns for the shepherd in 10:1-5 written plain
decisions.reason: As in English: in 10:1-5 the shepherd is a figure in a picture (10:6), so his pronouns take no deity_pronoun setting; pronouns for Jesus from 10:6 on do.

decisions.choice: le abre la puerta (B); cada una de sus ovejas (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: says what is opened and that each sheep is called (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: écoutent (B, R); entendent (L)
decisions.reason: As in 8:43-47: French "entendre" is to hear, "écouter" to listen. Hearing the shepherd's voice here means responding to it (meaning decision m3), so Balanced and Readable say "écouter"; Literal keeps the plain verb. As in English, the shepherd's pronouns in 10:1-5 are those of a figure in the picture and take no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "음성을 듣는다" (L); "목소리를 알아듣는다" (B); "목소리에 귀를 기울인다" (R)
decisions.reason: Korean "음성" is the familiar written word for a voice; Balanced and Readable use the everyday "목소리", and their verbs bring out the meaning decision: the sheep listen and respond.

decisions.choice: "người" (lowercase, no span) for the shepherd in 10:1-5
decisions.reason: The shepherd of the picture is referred to with the respectful neutral "người", without a deity_pronoun span, as the English leaves his pronouns plain; Jesus himself takes the span from 10:6 on.

decisions.choice: "gọi đích danh" for "calls by name"
decisions.reason: "gọi đích danh" is the natural Vietnamese idiom for calling someone by their own name.

source.text: ὅταν τὰ ἴδια πάντα ἐκβάλῃ, ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν πορεύεται, καὶ τὰ πρόβατα αὐτῷ ἀκολουθεῖ, ὅτι οἴδασιν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: When the own all he puts out, ahead of them he goes, and the sheep him follow, because they know the voice of him;

en.L: When he has put out all his own, he goes ahead of them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.
en.B: Once he has brought all his own sheep out, he walks on ahead, and the sheep follow him because they know his voice.
en.R: When all his own sheep are out, he walks in front of them. The sheep follow him, because they know his voice.

es.L: Cuando ha sacado a todas las suyas, va delante de ellas, y las ovejas lo siguen, porque conocen su voz.
es.B: Cuando ya ha sacado a todas sus ovejas, camina delante de ellas, y las ovejas lo siguen porque conocen su voz.
es.R: Cuando todas sus ovejas están fuera, camina delante de ellas. Las ovejas lo siguen, porque conocen su voz.

fr.L: Quand il a mis dehors toutes les siennes, il marche devant elles, et les brebis le suivent, parce qu’elles connaissent sa voix.
fr.B: Une fois qu’il a fait sortir toutes ses brebis, il marche devant elles, et les brebis le suivent parce qu’elles connaissent sa voix.
fr.R: Quand toutes ses brebis sont dehors, il marche devant elles. Les brebis le suivent, parce qu’elles connaissent sa voix.

sw.L: Akishawatoa nje wote walio wake, hutangulia mbele yao, na kondoo humfuata, kwa sababu wanaijua sauti yake.
sw.B: Akishawatoa nje kondoo wake wote, hutembea mbele yao, na kondoo humfuata kwa sababu wanaijua sauti yake.
sw.R: Kondoo wake wote wakishatoka nje, hutembea mbele yao. Kondoo humfuata, kwa sababu wanaijua sauti yake.

vi.L: Khi người đã đưa ra hết thảy [chiên] của mình, người đi trước chúng, và chiên đi theo người, vì chúng biết tiếng người.
vi.B: Khi đã đưa hết chiên của mình ra ngoài, người đi trước, và chiên theo sau người vì chúng biết tiếng người.
vi.R: Khi tất cả chiên của mình đã ra ngoài, người đi phía trước chúng. Chiên đi theo người, vì chúng biết tiếng người.

ko.L: 자기 것들을 모두 밖으로 내보내면, 그는 그들 앞에서 가고, 양들은 그를 따른다. 그들이 그의 음성을 알기 때문이다.
ko.B: 자기 양들을 다 밖으로 내보낸 다음 그는 앞장서서 가고, 양들은 그의 목소리를 알기 때문에 그를 따라간다.
ko.R: 자기 양들이 다 밖으로 나오면 그는 앞장서서 걸어간다. 양들은 그의 목소리를 알기 때문에 그를 따라간다.

decisions.choice: put out: bring out, with the sense of getting every one of them out
decisions.reason: The verb often means to throw or drive out, and it is the word used in 9:34-35 when the Pharisees threw the healed man out. Here the shepherd puts his own sheep out of the fold; what the authorities did to the man in hostility, the shepherd does for his flock's good. The force here is not violence but making sure that all his own are out.

decisions.choice: the shepherd walks in front and the sheep follow
alternatives: the shepherd drives the flock from behind
decisions.reason: Shepherds in the land of Israel led their flocks from the front, calling to them, and the sheep followed the voice they knew. The picture of a shepherd going before his flock is used of God (Psalm 80:2; Isaiah 40:11).

decisions.choice: because they know his voice: knowing his voice is the reason they follow
decisions.reason: The sheep do not follow because they are forced but because they recognise the one who calls them, which prepares for 10:14 ("I know my own and my own know me").

decisions.choice: all his own sheep; brought ... out (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "all his own"; Balanced and Readable supply "sheep", which the context makes clear, and use the gentler "brought out" for the verb (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: todas las suyas (L)
decisions.reason: Spanish "las suyas" is feminine, agreeing with "ovejas", so Literal can leave the noun unsaid as the Greek does; Balanced and Readable say "ovejas".

decisions.choice: mis dehors (L); fait sortir (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 9:34-35 when the Pharisees threw the man out, but here it has no violence in it (meaning decision m1). Literal says "mettre dehors", which keeps a link with "jeter dehors" without the force; Balanced uses the gentler "faire sortir", as in verse 3.

source.text: ἀλλοτρίῳ δὲ οὐ μὴ ἀκολουθήσουσιν ἀλλὰ φεύξονται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδασι τῶν ἀλλοτρίων τὴν φωνήν.

ko.L: 그러나 낯선 사람은 결코 따라가지 않고 오히려 그에게서 도망칠 것이다. 그들이 낯선 사람들의 음성을 알지 못하기 때문이다."
ko.B: 양들은 낯선 사람은 결코 따라가지 않고 그에게서 달아날 것이다. 낯선 사람들의 목소리를 알지 못하기 때문이다."
ko.R: 양들은 낯선 사람은 절대로 따라가지 않는다. 오히려 그 사람을 피해 도망간다. 낯선 사람의 목소리는 모르기 때문이다."

decisions.choice: a strong denial: they will certainly not follow
alternatives: a simple future: they will not follow
decisions.reason: The Greek puts two negatives together, the strongest way to deny something in the future.

decisions.choice: stranger: someone who does not belong to them
decisions.reason: The word means someone who belongs to another, not to this flock. It is not a foreigner by nation but a voice the sheep do not recognise as their shepherd's.

decisions.choice: the picture fits the man in chapter 9: he would not follow the Pharisees but listened to Jesus
alternatives: no connection with the preceding story
decisions.reason: The man born blind refused to be led by the Pharisees who questioned him (9:27-33), was thrown out (9:34), and then heard Jesus and worshiped him (9:35-38). The picture describes what has just happened, though Jesus does not name him.

decisions.choice: not ... at all (B); never (R); run (away)
decisions.reason: Plain words for the strong denial (meaning decision m1) and for fleeing.

decisions.choice: de ningún modo (L); jamás (B); nunca (R)
decisions.reason: Plain words for the strong denial (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "nhất định không" for the double negative
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has no double-negative emphasis; "nhất định không" gives the strong denial at Literal.

source.text: ταύτην τὴν παροιμίαν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· ἐκεῖνοι δὲ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τίνα ἦν ἃ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: This the figure said to them the Jesus; those but not understood what were [the things] which he was speaking to them.

en.L: Jesus told them this figure of speech, but they did not understand what the things were that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them.
en.B: Jesus spoke this figure of speech to them, but they did not grasp what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant by it.
en.R: Jesus used this picture to teach them, but they did not understand what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant.

fr.R: Jésus s’est servi de cette image pour les enseigner, mais ils n’ont pas compris ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} voulait dire.

vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói lời ví von này với họ, nhưng họ không hiểu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn nói gì.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu dùng hình ảnh này để dạy họ, nhưng họ không hiểu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn nói gì.

ko.L: 예수께서 그들에게 이 비유를 말씀하셨다. 그러나 그들은 그분이 자기들에게 말씀하시는 것들이 무엇인지 깨닫지 못했다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 이 비유를 말씀하셨지만, 그들은 그분이 무슨 뜻으로 하신 말씀인지 깨닫지 못했다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 이런 그림 같은 이야기로 그들을 가르치셨다. 그러나 그들은 그 말씀이 무슨 뜻인지 알지 못했다.

decisions.choice: a figure of speech: a saying with a hidden meaning that has to be worked out
alternatives: a parable in the sense of the stories in the other Gospels
decisions.reason: This is not the word the other Gospels use for Jesus's parables. It means a veiled or figurative saying, and in the Greek Old Testament it is used for proverbs. John uses it again when Jesus promises that he will no longer speak in figures but plainly (16:25, 29). Here it describes the picture of 10:1-5, whose meaning Jesus has not yet given.

decisions.choice: them: the Pharisees of 9:40-41
decisions.reason: The emphatic "those" points back to the people Jesus has been speaking to, the Pharisees who said, "We are not blind too, are we?" (9:40). Those who claim to see do not understand.

decisions.choice: they did not understand what his words meant
alternatives: they did not hear what he said
decisions.reason: They heard the words but did not grasp what they referred to, as often in John (8:27; 12:16). This is why Jesus goes on to explain (10:7).

decisions.choice: figure of speech (L, B); picture (R)
decisions.reason: "Parable" would bring in the word of the other Gospels, which John does not use (meaning decision m1). Readable uses a plain word for the same thing.

decisions.choice: Jesus told them (L); Jesus spoke ... to them (B)
alternatives: This figure of speech Jesus told them
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "this figure" first for emphasis; English puts the subject first, and Literal follows English order here because the fronted object reads awkwardly.

decisions.choice: figura (L, B); imagen (R)
decisions.reason: "Parábola" would bring in the word of the other Gospels, which John does not use (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the Greek order, with "esta figura" first.

decisions.choice: parole figurée (L); langage figuré (B); image (R)
decisions.reason: The word is not the "parable" of the other Gospels but a veiled saying whose sense has to be worked out (meaning decision m1). French uses the same words as in 16:25 and 16:29, where the Greek word returns, so that the link stays visible.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the narration of this passage (10:6-7): the passé simple ("Jésus leur dit", "ils ne comprirent pas") at Literal and Balanced, the tense of written narrative, and the passé composé ("ils n’ont pas compris") at Readable, the past tense young readers know. Literal keeps the Greek order, with the figure placed first for emphasis, which French allows by taking it up again with "la".

decisions.choice: mfano (L, B); picha (R)
decisions.reason: παροιμίαν is a saying with a hidden meaning. "Methali" is a proverb and "fumbo" a riddle; "mfano" (figure, comparison) is the usual word for a picture-saying like this one. Readable says "picha" (picture), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun span in Korean; respect for Jesus is carried by "께서", the honorific -시- and "그분"
alternatives: a deity_pronoun span as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7). This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "비유" (L, B); "그림 같은 이야기" (R)
decisions.reason: The word means a saying whose meaning must be worked out. "비유" is the ordinary Korean word for such a figure; Readable describes it in plain words.

decisions.choice: "lời ví von" for paroimia
decisions.reason: "lời ví von" is an everyday word for a figurative saying whose meaning must be worked out; "ngụ ngôn" suggests a fable or parable story, which this is not.

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}" for Jesus in the narrative
decisions.reason: Style guide sections 6-7: the narrator refers to Jesus as "Ngài", with the capital as the reader setting.

vi.B: Vậy Đức Giê-xu lại nói với họ: "Thật vậy, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là cửa cho chiên.
vi.R: Vì thế Đức Giê-xu lại nói với họ: "Ta nói thật với các người: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là cửa cho chiên ra vào.

ko.L: 그러므로 예수께서 다시 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 나는 양들의 문이다.
ko.B: 그래서 예수께서 다시 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "진실로 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 나는 양들을 위한 문이다.
ko.R: 그래서 예수께서 다시 말씀하셨다. "내가 분명히 말한다. 나는 양들이 드나드는 문이다.

decisions.choice: the door of the sheep (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the shepherd of the sheep (one early papyrus, P75, and some Coptic witnesses)
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts read "the door". A few early witnesses, the papyrus P75 among them, read "the shepherd", which is probably a change to fit 10:11. "The door" is the harder reading and is supported by 10:9. A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the door for the sheep: the door by which the sheep go in and out
alternatives: the door to the sheep, by which shepherds come to them
decisions.reason: In verses 1-2 the door is the way the shepherd comes to the sheep; in verse 9 it is the way the sheep go in and out. Jesus is the second here, as verse 9 makes plain, but the first is not excluded: those who came another way (verse 8) did not come through him.

decisions.choice: I am with a predicate: one of the sayings in which Jesus says who he is
alternatives: an echo of the divine name
decisions.reason: With a predicate the words are ordinary grammar. It is one of a series of such sayings (6:35; 8:12; 10:9, 11; 11:25; 14:6; 15:1), in which Jesus takes a picture and says that he is what it points to.

decisions.choice: so ... again: because they did not understand, he speaks again and explains
decisions.reason: The connecting word ties this to 10:6: Jesus explains the figure, taking up its parts one by one, first the door and then (10:11) the shepherd.

decisions.choice: the door of the sheep (L); the door for the sheep (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show which door is meant (meaning decision m2). "Door" is kept at every level, as in 10:1-2.

decisions.choice: la puerta de las ovejas (L); la puerta para las ovejas (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: shows which door is meant (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "양들이 드나드는 문" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the meaning decision: the door by which the sheep go in and out. Literal "양들의 문" and Balanced "양들을 위한 문" follow the English levels.

decisions.choice: "cửa cho chiên ra vào" (the door the sheep go in and out by)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "cửa của chiên" could sound like a door the sheep own; R spells out the meaning decision (the door by which the sheep go in and out).

source.text: πάντες ὅσοι ἦλθον πρὸ ἐμοῦ κλέπται εἰσὶν καὶ λῃσταί· ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἤκουσαν αὐτῶν τὰ πρόβατα.

records.literal_gloss: All as many as came before me thieves are and bandits; but not heard them the sheep.

en.B: All who came before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} are thieves and bandits, but the sheep did not give them a hearing.
en.R: All who came before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, claiming to be shepherds, are thieves and bandits. But the sheep did not listen to them.

es.L: Todos los que vinieron antes de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} son ladrones y bandidos; pero las ovejas no los oyeron.

vi.B: Tất cả những kẻ đã đến trước {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đều là kẻ trộm và kẻ cướp, nhưng chiên đã không nghe theo chúng.
vi.R: Tất cả những kẻ đến trước {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, tự xưng là người chăn, đều là kẻ trộm và kẻ cướp. Nhưng chiên không nghe theo chúng.

ko.L: 나보다 먼저 온 자들은 모두 도둑들이고 강도들이다. 그러나 양들은 그들[의 말]을 듣지 않았다.
ko.B: 나보다 먼저 온 사람들은 모두 도둑이고 강도다. 그러나 양들은 그들의 말을 들어 주지 않았다.
ko.R: 자기가 목자라고 하며 나보다 먼저 온 사람들은 모두 도둑이고 강도다. 그러나 양들은 그들의 말을 듣지 않았다.

decisions.choice: all who came before me: those who came claiming to lead God's people in his place, not Moses and the prophets
alternatives: every teacher and prophet before Jesus
only the Pharisees of his own day
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the prophets with respect: Moses wrote about him (5:46), Abraham rejoiced to see his day (8:56), and Isaiah saw his glory (12:41). The ones meant are those who came to the flock by another way, as in verse 1: leaders who used the people for themselves, like the shepherds of Ezekiel 34, and men who claimed to be the deliverer and led people into ruin. The present tense "are" may point especially to leaders still at work, such as those who had just thrown out the healed man. Who exactly is meant is not stated.

decisions.choice: before me (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the words left out (some early manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Some early witnesses leave out "before me", probably to avoid the impression that Jesus condemned the prophets; without them the sentence reads "All who came are thieves and bandits". The SBLGNT keeps the words. A reviewer should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: did not hear them: did not listen to them or follow them
alternatives: did not hear the sound of their voices
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, hearing means responding. The true sheep did not follow them, as the sheep in verse 5 flee from a stranger.

decisions.choice: claiming to be shepherds
decisions.reason: Readable makes explicit who "came": not everyone who lived earlier, but those who came to the flock as leaders (meaning decision m1). This goes beyond what the Greek says and reflects the uncertain decision m1.

decisions.choice: before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}
decisions.reason: From here Jesus applies the picture to himself, so "me" takes the deity_pronoun span (see 10:3).

decisions.choice: diciendo que eran pastores
decisions.reason: As in English: makes explicit who "came" (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: antes de mí
decisions.reason: From here Jesus applies the picture to himself, so the stressed "mí" takes the setting.

decisions.choice: "그들[의 말]을 듣지 않았다"
decisions.reason: Korean does not "hear" a person; the object is the person's words, supplied in brackets at Literal.

source.text: ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ θύρα· δι’ ἐμοῦ ἐάν τις εἰσέλθῃ σωθήσεται καὶ εἰσελεύσεται καὶ ἐξελεύσεται καὶ νομὴν εὑρήσει.

records.literal_gloss: I am the door; through me if anyone enters he will be saved and will go in and will go out and pasture will find.

en.L: I am the door; through {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, if anyone enters, {{gender:they|he}} will be saved, and will go in and will go out and will find pasture.
en.B: I am the door. If anyone goes in through {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{gender:they|he}} will be saved, going in and going out and finding pasture.
en.R: I am the door. If anyone comes in through {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{gender:they|he}} will be saved. {{gender:They|He}} will go in and out, and will find good grass to eat.

es.L: Yo soy la puerta; por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, si alguien entra, será salvo, y entrará y saldrá, y hallará pastos.
es.B: Yo soy la puerta. Si alguien entra por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, será salvo; entrará y saldrá, y encontrará pastos.
es.R: Yo soy la puerta. Si alguien entra por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, se salvará. Podrá entrar y salir, y encontrará buen pasto para comer.

fr.L: Je suis la porte ; par {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, si quelqu’un entre, il sera sauvé, et il entrera et sortira, et il trouvera [un] pâturage.
fr.B: Je suis la porte. Si quelqu’un entre en passant par {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, il sera sauvé ; il ira et viendra, et trouvera un pâturage.
fr.R: Je suis la porte. Si quelqu’un entre en passant par {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, il sera sauvé. Il pourra aller et venir, et il trouvera de la bonne herbe à manger.

sw.L: Mimi ni mlango; kupitia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, mtu yeyote akiingia, ataokolewa, naye ataingia na kutoka na kupata malisho.
sw.B: Mimi ni mlango. Mtu yeyote akiingia kupitia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, ataokolewa, akiingia na kutoka na kupata malisho.
sw.R: Mimi ni mlango. Mtu yeyote akiingia kupitia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, ataokolewa. Ataingia na kutoka, na atapata majani mazuri ya kula.

vi.L: Ta là cửa; qua {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nếu ai vào, người ấy sẽ được cứu, và sẽ vào, sẽ ra, và sẽ tìm được đồng cỏ.
vi.B: Ta là cửa. Ai vào qua {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được cứu; người ấy sẽ ra vào và tìm được đồng cỏ.
vi.R: Ta là cửa. Ai đi vào qua {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được cứu. Người ấy sẽ được ra vào, và sẽ tìm được cỏ xanh để ăn.

ko.L: 나는 문이다. 나를 통하여 누구든지 들어가면 구원을 받을 것이고, 들어가고 나가며 풀밭을 찾을 것이다.
ko.B: 나는 문이다. 누구든지 나를 통해 들어오면 구원을 받을 것이다. 그는 들어가고 나가며 풀밭을 찾을 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 문이다. 누구든지 나를 통해 들어오면 구원을 받는다. 그 사람은 마음 놓고 드나들며 먹을 풀을 찾을 것이다.

decisions.choice: will be saved: kept safe and given life, as a sheep in the fold and as a person who comes to Jesus
decisions.reason: In the picture the sheep that comes in by the door is safe from thieves. Applied to people, being saved in John means being rescued from perishing and given eternal life (3:16-17; 5:34; 12:47). Both are in view.

decisions.choice: go in and go out: live freely and safely
decisions.reason: Going in and going out is a Hebrew way of speaking of the whole of a person's life and daily movement (Deuteronomy 28:6; Psalm 121:8). Moses asked for a leader who would go out and come in before the people, so that they would not be like sheep without a shepherd (Numbers 27:17).

decisions.choice: find pasture: the shepherd's provision, as in Psalm 23 and Ezekiel 34
decisions.reason: God leads his flock to green pastures (Psalm 23:2) and promises to feed his sheep in good pasture on the mountains of Israel (Ezekiel 34:14).

decisions.choice: through me: placed first for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "through me" before "if anyone enters": it is through him, and no other way (verse 1), that anyone comes in.

decisions.choice: anyone ... {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: "Anyone" means any person, man or woman; the following pronoun takes the gender setting, with "he" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: good grass to eat
decisions.reason: Readable says what pasture is for sheep, a place to graze.

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: "Si alguien entra ... será salvo" needs no pronoun in Spanish, so no setting applies.

decisions.choice: por mí, si alguien entra (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "por mí" first, as the Greek does for emphasis.

decisions.choice: no gender setting: "si quelqu’un ..., il"
decisions.reason: English puts "they/he" under the gender setting. As in 8:51, French "il" taking up "quelqu’un" is the grammatical agreement and reads as anyone at all; a doubled "il ou elle" would be heavy in a saying meant for every hearer.

decisions.choice: il ira et viendra (B); il pourra aller et venir (R); il entrera et sortira (L)
decisions.reason: "Going in and going out" is a Hebrew way of speaking of a whole life lived freely and safely (meaning decision m2). French "aller et venir" is the everyday phrase for moving about freely, so Balanced and Readable use it; Literal keeps the two verbs of the Greek.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "누구든지" (anyone) and an unexpressed or neutral subject ("그 사람")
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean "누구든지" is already inclusive and needs no pronoun after it, so there are not two ways of saying the same thing (style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: "마음 놓고 드나들며" (go in and out without fear)
decisions.reason: Readable adds 마음 놓고 to carry the meaning decision on the idiom: to live freely and safely.

decisions.choice: "ai ... người ấy" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender setting span as in English
decisions.reason: Style guide section 7: "ai" (anyone) and "người ấy" (that person) are already inclusive in Vietnamese, so the English gender setting has no counterpart here.

source.text: ὁ κλέπτης οὐκ ἔρχεται εἰ μὴ ἵνα κλέψῃ καὶ θύσῃ καὶ ἀπολέσῃ· ἐγὼ ἦλθον ἵνα ζωὴν ἔχωσιν καὶ περισσὸν ἔχωσιν.

records.literal_gloss: The thief not comes except that he may steal and slaughter and destroy; I came that life they may have and abundance they may have.

en.L: The thief does not come except to steal and slaughter and destroy; I came that they may have life and may have [it] beyond measure.
en.B: The thief comes for no other reason than to steal and slaughter and destroy. I came so that they may have life, and have it in overflowing measure.
en.R: A thief has only one reason for coming: to steal the sheep, kill them and destroy them. But I came so that they can have life, life that overflows.

es.L: El ladrón no viene sino para robar y matar y destruir; yo vine para que tengan vida, y [la] tengan en abundancia.
es.B: El ladrón no viene más que a robar, matar y destruir. Yo he venido para que tengan vida, y la tengan en abundancia.
es.R: El ladrón viene solo para una cosa: robar las ovejas, matarlas y destruirlas. Pero yo vine para que tengan vida, una vida que rebosa.

fr.L: Le voleur ne vient pas, sinon pour voler, égorger et faire périr ; {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je suis venu pour qu’elles aient [la] vie et qu’elles [l’]aient au-delà de toute mesure.
fr.B: Le voleur ne vient que pour voler, égorger et faire périr. Moi, je suis venu pour que les brebis aient la vie, et qu’elles l’aient à profusion.
fr.R: Un voleur vient pour une seule raison : voler les brebis, les tuer et les faire périr. Mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je suis venu pour que les brebis aient la vie, une vie qui déborde.

sw.L: Mwizi haji ila ili aibe na kuchinja na kuharibu; mimi nilikuja ili wawe na uzima, na wawe nao kwa wingi kupita kiasi.
sw.B: Mwizi huja kwa sababu moja tu: kuiba, kuchinja na kuharibu. Mimi nimekuja ili wawe na uzima, nao uwe tele kwao.
sw.R: Mwizi ana sababu moja tu ya kuja: kuiba kondoo, kuwaua na kuwaangamiza. Lakini mimi nimekuja ili wapate uzima, uzima unaofurika.

vi.L: Kẻ trộm không đến, ngoại trừ để trộm, làm thịt và hủy diệt; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đến để chúng có sự sống và có [sự sống ấy] một cách dồi dào.
vi.B: Kẻ trộm đến chỉ để trộm cắp, giết thịt và hủy diệt. Ta đã đến để chúng có sự sống, và có sự sống ấy tràn đầy.
vi.R: Kẻ trộm đến chỉ vì một lý do: để bắt trộm chiên, giết chúng và tiêu diệt chúng. Còn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến để chúng có sự sống, một sự sống tràn đầy.

ko.L: 도둑은 훔치고 도살하고 멸하려는 것이 아니면 오지 않는다. 나는 그들이 생명을 가지고, 넘치도록 [그것을] 가지게 하려고 왔다.
ko.B: 도둑은 오직 훔치고 잡아 죽이고 없애 버리려고 온다. 나는 그들이 생명을 얻고, 그 생명이 차고 넘치게 하려고 왔다.
ko.R: 도둑이 오는 이유는 하나뿐이다. 양을 훔치고, 죽이고, 없애 버리려는 것이다. 그러나 나는 양들이 생명을 얻고, 그 생명이 넘쳐흐르게 하려고 왔다.

decisions.choice: slaughter: kill as an animal is killed for its meat
decisions.reason: The verb is used of killing animals, often in sacrifice, and of slaughtering for food (Luke 15:23). In a picture of sheep the sense is butchering; there is no thought of sacrifice here.

decisions.choice: destroy and life: perishing and eternal life
alternatives: physical harm and physical life only
decisions.reason: The verb "destroy" is the one John uses for perishing (3:16; 10:28), and the life Jesus gives is eternal life, which begins now (3:15-16; 5:24; 10:28). The thief brings the sheep to ruin; Jesus came to give them life that does not end.

decisions.choice: more than enough: life in full measure, beyond what is needed
decisions.reason: The word means what goes beyond the measure, an overflowing amount. It describes the fullness of the life Jesus gives, not wealth or comfort. The contrast is with shepherds who fed themselves instead of the flock (Ezekiel 34:2-3).

decisions.choice: the thief comes only to ...; I came that ...: two comings set against each other
decisions.reason: The construction "not ... except" limits the thief's purpose to harm. Jesus's "I came" answers it and recalls "all who came before me" (verse 8).

decisions.choice: beyond measure (L); in overflowing measure (B); life that overflows (R)
decisions.reason: These words say what the Greek word says, an amount that goes past the measure (meaning decision m3), without the wording familiar from other versions. Literal brackets "it", which the Greek leaves understood.

decisions.choice: to steal the sheep, kill them and destroy them
alternatives: to steal and kill and destroy
decisions.reason: Readable supplies the sheep as the object, which the picture implies.

decisions.choice: en abundancia (L, B); una vida que rebosa (R)
decisions.reason: An amount that goes past the measure (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: las ovejas
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable supplies the object the picture implies.

decisions.choice: faire périr; au-delà de toute mesure (L), à profusion (B), une vie qui déborde (R)
decisions.reason: "Faire périr" keeps the verb John uses for perishing (3:16, "ne périsse pas"; meaning decision m2). For the last word each level says what the Greek says, an amount past the measure (meaning decision m3), without the wording familiar from other French versions.

decisions.choice: "생명" (life) at every level; "넘치도록" (L), "차고 넘치게" (B), "넘쳐흐르게" (R)
decisions.reason: zoe is "생명" throughout John (style guide, section 6), not "삶" (a way of living). The overflow is said with native Korean verbs.

decisions.choice: "양을 훔치고" and "양들이" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the sheep, keeping the picture explicit for new readers.

decisions.choice: "làm thịt" (L), "giết thịt" (B) for thyō
decisions.reason: The verb is killing an animal for its meat; "làm thịt" / "giết thịt" keep that picture, which fits a thief taking sheep.

decisions.choice: "dồi dào" (L); "tràn đầy" (B, R) for perisson
decisions.reason: "dư dật" is the familiar older wording and now sounds dated; "dồi dào" and "tràn đầy" are modern words for life in full measure.
